note: Part 4 FIRE inside the demo at an arbitrary frame (verify.sh shoots 70M cycles on both models). Frame-independent checks only: the fire is seeded by an LFSR and the palette switches every 200 frames, so no cell colour and no single palette can be pinned; the chain moves two phase steps a frame, so no glyph box can be pinned either. Kept from the 2026-09-23 pin (I-008): border black, seed row burning, lower ten rows carrying the fire. Added 2026-09-24 with the max-out: every lit pixel in the fire rows is a colour of one of the four palettes (0 9 2 8 10 7 1; 6 14 3 15 1; 6 5 3 13 1; 6 4 10 15 1), which also holds across a switch since both palettes in flight are in the union; and the sprite band, lines 60 to 150 where the chain lives (Y 64 to 127 plus 21 rows), carries at least 150 lit pixels that are either a fire colour or the chain's yellow. Six glyphs of 100 to 250 pixels each never all leave that band. Yellow is also in palette 0, so the band check cannot tell a glyph from a warm flame by colour; the standalone pin (test/expect-p4.json) does that by box.
